research_rationale: EO 11708 (signed 1973-03-23; 38 FR 7979-7980, Federal Register of March 27, 1973, PDF pages 11-12) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (registered as ORIGINAL:EO:11708). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 11708, Placing Certain Positions in Levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule, dated March 23, 1973, under section 5317 of title 5. The dossier inventory of 25 clauses (Section 1 with items (1)-(14), Section 2 with items (1)-(8), Section 3) was checked against the numbered text and is confirmed complete. The order has three operative parts: Sec. 1 places fourteen positions in level IV, Sec. 2 continues eight positions in level V, and Sec. 3 revokes EO 11248 except for the Section 2 positions. First and whole-order end: express supersession by EO 11768 of February 20, 1974 (39 FR 6693), Sec. 4, effective on signing, 1974-02-20. Earlier ends of single clauses: items (6) and (7) of Section 1 were deleted by EO 11727 Sec. 4, effective as of 1973-07-01 (Sec. 6); item (8) of Section 2 was deleted by EO 11715 Sec. 2 on 1973-04-24; Section 3 was a self-executing revocation performed on 1973-03-23. Amendments that strike and insert text (EO 11715 items (8), (9), (10); EO 11736 items (2), (4), (14)) are later events and the clauses continue, amended, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, with the before and after text recorded on each clause. Additions (items (15) to (18) of Section 1 and a new item (8) of Section 2) are amendments of the lead clauses of their sections. The whole-order end is the latest first end, 1974-02-20. Searches: the held-text search of the number 11708 returned the orders above and later orders that recite EO 11708 as amended or superseded (EO 11727 Sec. 4 recitals aside, EO 11768 Sec. 4); the packet's machine searches (current-law:usc one lead, which is the printed text of EO 11727 in a note to 21 U.S.C. 801; current-law:ecfr none; later-events:ofr_catalog five leads) were read with their coverage notes and name no other instrument; the 1989 OFR codification row reads, in substance, that the order was amended by EOs 11715, 11727 and 11736 and superseded by EO 11768. The later orders that were not APP-only are cited by their official Federal Register texts (ACTOR_TEXT:EO:11715, EO:11727, EO:11736, EO:11768); no transcription is relied on for any quoted text.
savings_reason: EO 11768 supersedes EO 11708 as amended without saving any of its placements. Its own Sec. 3 protects the appointment of an incumbent from being terminated or requiring reappointment by reason of EO 11768; appointments are not created by EO 11708, so that is not a residual of the superseded order. Where EO 11768 places the same positions in level IV or V again, the pay level rests on EO 11768 as the successor authority, not on EO 11708 or its amending orders. The revocation of EO 11248 performed by EO 11708 Sec. 3 stays performed (EO 11248 was revoked, except for the Section 2 positions), and the held text of EO 11768 does not revive EO 11248. No other savings, transfer or accrued-right provision is found in the held text of EO 11768.

research_rationale: EO 11812 (signed 1974-10-07; 39 FR 36307, Federal Register of October 8, 1974, PDF pages 199-204) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (registered as ORIGINAL:EO:11812; OCR of the 1974 scan, with garbled digits in places). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 11812, Adjusting the Rates of Basic Pay, Basic Allowance for Subsistence and Basic Allowance for Quarters for Members of the Uniformed Services, dated October 7, 1974. The dossier inventory is corrected: its Section 2 clause ran Sections 2, 3 and 4 together, and the OCR's two adjacent headings 'S E C . 5 .' and 'S E C . 6 .' had made the supersession list a mislabelled Section 6 with items (1)-(7). The corrected inventory has six clauses: Sec. 1 (basic pay tables), Sec. 2 (subsistence allowance), Sec. 3 (quarters allowance), Sec. 4 (level V limit), Sec. 5 (supersession of seven earlier orders), Sec. 6 (effective date October 1, 1974). First and whole-order end: express supersession by EO 11883 of October 6, 1975 (40 FR 47091), Sec. 5, whose Sec. 4 makes the replacement uniformed-service rates effective October 1, 1975; the Sec. 1-4 clauses end 1975-10-01 (alternative reading 1975-10-06, stated in each reason), and the Sec. 5 and Sec. 6 clauses were exhausted when the order was signed on 1974-10-07 (alternative reading: its retroactive effective date 1974-10-01), so the whole-order end is 1975-10-01, the latest first end. Authority: the order rests on 37 U.S.C. 1009 as added by Public Law 93-419 of September 19, 1974 (88 Stat. 1152, held at jobs/selden-statutes/output/texts/STATUTE-88-Pg1152.txt), under which each adjustment has the force of law and carries the effective date of the General Schedule adjustment; that statute is the authority, not an ending instrument (the dossier note that its acting text did not match by number reflects that the statute does not mention this order). The tracker's QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT for this order is a Stage 19 count outside this claim; the held-text search of the order number finds only EO 11883 (Sec. 5) and its printed FR text, and the packet's machine searches (current-law:usc one lead, current-law:ecfr none, later-events:ofr_catalog two leads) were read with their coverage notes and name no earlier or other instrument. The original is the official FR text, so no transcription is relied on for it.
savings_reason: EO 11883 Sec. 2 adjusts again, under section 1009 of title 37, the same uniformed-service rates of monthly basic pay, basic allowance for subsistence and basic allowance for quarters from October 1, 1975, so the adjustment function continues under the successor order; pay and allowances that accrued at EO 11812's rates for periods before October 1, 1975 stay due as accrued entitlements, and the held text of EO 11883 contains no provision cancelling them. The supersession of the seven earlier orders listed in EO 11812 Sec. 5 is an accrued effect: EO 11883 does not name, revive or amend any of them. Section 5 of EO 11883 supersedes only Executive Order No. 11811 and Executive Order No. 11812, and the held text of EO 11883 has no exception or pending-matter clause for either.

research_rationale: EO 12162 (signed 1979-09-28, 44 FR 56665, Federal Register of October 2, 1979) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12162.txt, registered as ORIGINAL:EO:12162). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979, titled Amendment to Executive Order 12140, signed at The White House on September 28, 1979. The order is a single operative paragraph: acting under the Constitution, the statutes and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, it amends Executive Order No. 12140, in the words of the held text, "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." The held text of EO 12140 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12140.txt, 44 FR 31159) shows that first sentence provided that the order terminates, unless extended, at midnight on September 30, 1979 (paraphrased, not quoted), so the amendment removed 12140's own sunset two days before it would have run; the second sentence (the Secretary of Energy may revoke the delegation) was left in place. The amendment is performed in the present tense by the order itself, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1979-09-28; the consequence (EO 12140 no longer terminating on 1979-09-30) is a surviving effect recorded in the savings statement, not a continuing command of EO 12162. The later express revocation by EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237) is recorded as a later event and is not the first end, because a later revocation does not prove first cessation of a command already performed (owner ruling 2026-10-28, points 1 and 3). The dossier question 'target provision not located: EO:12553' is answered: the held text of EO 12553 lists 12162 in its table of revoked orders. Own-terms: no sunset, condition or duration in the order. The packet's machine searches (current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr, no hits for this order; later-events:ofr_catalog, two leads, both the EO 12553 note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986') were read with their coverage notes and surfaced no earlier instrument. The only other held-text citation of the number, FRDOC 97-2965, mentions "Executive Order 12162, Federalism, dated October 26, 1987", which is not this order (a different order number and subject) and is not a later event.
savings_reason: The amendment made by EO 12162 on 1979-09-28 is an accrued effect: EO 12140 was not terminated by its own first-sentence sunset on 1979-09-30 and continued as amended until it ended by some later act. EO 12553 revokes the Executive Orders it lists together with their amendments, and its table lists both 12140 and 12162; the held text of EO 12553 contains no exception, saving or pending-matter provision for either. The date and cause of the end of EO 12140 itself (the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act authority it rests on, or the 1986 revocation) is not established by a held source in this packet and is not asserted; it is the subject of EO 12140's own lifecycle, not of EO 12162's executed amendment.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held order texts for the number 12162 (cruden number search) and read the packet's later-events chain and OFR catalog lead: the only instrument naming this order as revoked is EO 12553 (1986-02-25). No instrument before 1979-09-28 can end an order not yet signed, and none between 1979-09-28 and 1986-02-25 amends, revokes or supersedes it. The order's own text carries no sunset or condition.
